analysis.title: Lev Fin Weekend Reading Observations: cold turkey
key_insights: AI jitters pushed the VIX to its 2026 high. S&P 500 fell 8.6% on the week into correction territory and the Nasdaq lost 10.4%, its worst weekly slide since March 2020.

HY spreads widened 51bps to +367bps, the largest weekly widening of 2026 and about double the prior yearly high of +27bps. IG widened 10bps but returned +0.84% on rates, versus a 0.86% loss for HY, the widest IG/HY weekly return gap this year.
HY breadth was poor: 1,753 of 1,934 HY bonds fell in price, so the week was market-driven rather than single-name driven.

Credit vs equities: HY cash widened 51bps against ~39bps implied by the 2026 norm of ~4.5bps per 1% S&P move, with double-Bs doing most of the catching up. CDX HY returned -1.4%, only a 1.1 standard deviation move over 15 years (44th worst week), so CDX lagged cash and equities.
Left tail: 65 bonds from 37 issuers fell 5+ points, versus 24 the prior week and the prior 2026 high of 41. More than half of the year's 488 such decliners have come since early October.
The left tail has broadened beyond triple-Cs: 45 of 65 decliners were single-B (37) or double-B (8), versus 18 the prior week.
Problem sectors are multiplying: Building Products and Cable (Cablevision and Cable One both entered grace periods on the same day), HY Financials (GSYCN, IEP, NAVINT), education and packaged foods.
Systemic stress is not yet signaled: 44.5% of HY still trades inside +200bps OAS, though that share fell 12.4pts on the week, the largest drop of 2026.
New issues turned: four of ten HY new issues finished below issue price after six weeks where all traded higher.

Software split: CCC Intelligent Solutions' $2.85bn LBO financing was the standout, with the $2.2bn TLB at S+375 @ 99.5 and the largest reverse flex since May. Proofpoint priced $1.25bn 8.5% secured notes due 2031 and a $735MM add-on. UST Global's $400MM loan was shelved.
73% of the $209bn of software loans in the Bloomberg Loan Index trade above 90, so pull-to-pars and refis are possible.

HY YTD return turned negative at -0.32% (from +0.54%) and triple-Cs hit -5.82% YTD. 354 HY bonds yield 10%+ (+40) and only 385 trade at or above par (-83). GIR forecasts a 4% USD HY default rate next year and prefers subordination premium over moving down in quality.
Consumer discretionary and staples Chapter 11 volume YTD is at six-year and ten-plus-year highs. AI took $355.9bn, 86% of US VC funding, in 1H26.

sector_views.rationale: GIR expects modest spread widening, 4% default rate and prefers selection from the top of the capital structure.
Pure-play scaled software deals drew strong demand even in a risk-off tape, while IT services is facing selectivity.

sector_views.sector: Cable, building products, education, packaged foods
sector_views.rationale: Weak earnings and sector-specific trends are driving distress and grace periods.

macro_indicators.interpretation: IG returned +0.84% as lower rates offset the spread widening.
GIR forecast supports preference for higher quality and subordination premium.

risk_factors: Further AI-driven equity selloff spilling into credit.
Broadening of problem sectors into systemic stress.
Weakening new issue market and shelved deals.
Rising defaults, with consumer Chapter 11s at multi-year highs.
FOMC minutes noting that almost all participants judged further rate hikes would likely be appropriate.
vol_and_positioning: VIX reached its highest level of 2026 on the week.
67% of HY funds have beaten their benchmarks YTD, helped by underweights in HY datacenter bonds and triple-Cs, per GIR.
Mutual funds and ETFs are generally underweight HY datacenter bonds.

tension_points.bull_case: Sector-specific weakness is not systemic, with 44.5% of HY still trading inside +200bps and scaled software financings clearing well.
tension_points.bear_case: More problem sectors are appearing, the left tail now includes single-B and double-B names, and new issues are trading below issue price.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued fall in the share of HY inside +200bps OAS beyond the 12.4pt weekly drop, and further problem sectors emerging.

theme_stances.key_argument: Spreads look cheaper but quality selection from the top of the capital structure is preferred over reaching for yield.
theme_stances.evidence: Plates should be built from the top of the table, not the bottom.
